rationale: The 0.5ms accepted-command control reproduces all 244 original shared states and the native failure diagnostic bit-identically. Halving dt alone passes unchanged native gates through the exact original failure endpoint; initial arm/finger changes are below 0.00044rad and maximum shared packet-center difference is 3.062mm. This bounded evidence is sufficient to prospectively test the numerical setting on forty fresh closed-loop identities, with all existing mechanical gates retained and stop-on-invalidity unchanged.
limitations: This is permission to collect qualification evidence, not full numerical convergence, validated tactile/contact force transfer, policy reliability, or hardware readiness. BoxBack collision remains at both timesteps. The original failed policy attempt remains invalid and unscored. The new cohort changes dt and native-start distribution, so do not pool its rate with the original screen or infer paired superiority over other models. Starts are stratified convenience samples, not training-unseen or representative lab frequencies. Actual settled states and technical validity must be audited per trial; no retries or replacement of failed identities. Real hardware latch remains 2.5N; simulated 1N proxy is exploratory.
